source: a gun game where at the start there will be three maps and whichever one has the most votes they will all teleport to and then be separated into 2 teams with all players each have 1 sniper infinite grenades 1 normal gun and a mini gun that can only be used for 30 secs and there will be a 130 second timer so whatever team has the most kills when the timer is out wins

answers.ask: What should the maps look like - military, urban, sci-fi, something else?
answers.answer: Use a military theme for all three maps, matching the gun-game combat.

answers.ask: Should all three maps share a lane layout, or should they differ (open, close-quarters, vertical)?
answers.answer: Have the three maps differ: one open, one close-quarters, and one with vertical areas, so the vote gives players distinct choices.

config.genre_evidence: "gun game" with "1 sniper," "1 normal gun," "a mini gun," two teams, and a win condition based on "the most kills" during a "130 second timer" describes a team deathmatch shooting arena. Map voting and timed rounds are secondary party/round-based features.
config.evidence: "separated into 2 teams" and "whatever team has the most kills when the timer is out wins"
config.addendum:
LAYOUT FEATURES for this Shooter map. Build these as the actual structure of the space rather than as set dressing, keep them visually distinct from one another, and keep the whole layout legible in one view.

SHAPE OF THE SPACE - Lane Network: Parallel routes, classically three, channelling team traffic into predictable engagement fronts.

INCLUDE:
- Opposing Team Bases: Balanced bases at opposite ends of the map, each enclosed so it is not overlooked from open ground.
- Tactical Cover Arrays: Waist-high (3–4 studs) and full-body (7–8 studs) cover distributed evenly across every lane.
- Lane Pinch Point: Narrow transitions where lanes meet, concentrating fights into contested ground.
